# Base URL ``` https://metrics-api.nanostream.cloud ``` > ⚠️ **Breaking change — v2.34.2:** The **domain** has changed and endpoint paths no longer include the `/api` prefix. > > **Before:** `https://metrics.nanocosmos.de/api/v2/...` > > **Now:** `https://metrics-api.nanostream.cloud/v2/...` # Info © 2026 nanocosmos GmbH. All Rights Reserved.

nanoStream Cloud Analytics offers a great way to monitor and analyze the performance and quality of service of your live streams.
This is the documentation for the direct access of the API.

You can access the UI [here](https://metrics.nanostream.cloud)
General documentation can be found on [https://docs.nanocosmos.de/docs/cloud/analytics](https://docs.nanocosmos.de/docs/cloud/analytics) ## How to authenticate on this page to test the API routes? First use the authentication route to get a token which you must paste after clicking on "Authorize" on the top of this page. You can only use the metric routes after successful authentication! ## API Status Codes The API responses always contain one of these general status codes to provide additional information about the requested data: | Status Code | Label | Description | | ----------- | ----- | ----------- | | 1000 | OK | Success, related data was found. | | 2000 | NO DATA | Request was successful, but no related data was found. | | 2001 | NO ALERTS | Request was successful, but no alerts were found. This is used for requests regarding alert information retrieval. | Refer to the [documentation](https://docs.nanocosmos.de/docs/analytics/api-docs#api-status-codes) for more details. ## API request limiting This API limits requests to 1 per second but allows short bursts of up to 30 additional requests to be processed immediately without delay. If the rate limit is exceeded, you will receive a 502 (Bad Gateway) or 504 (Gateway Timeout) HTTP error code from Nginx.

Authentication with user credentials to get access token

403.description: Forbidden, account is disabled or unauthorized.

x-codeSamples.source:
curl --request POST \
  --url https://metrics-api.nanostream.cloud/authenticate \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"email":"foo@bar.foo","password":"secretFooBar"}'

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"net/http"
	"io/ioutil"
)

func main() {

	url := "https://metrics-api.nanostream.cloud/authenticate"

	payload := strings.NewReader("{\"email\":\"foo@bar.foo\",\"password\":\"secretFooBar\"}")

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, payload)

	req.Header.Add("content-type", "application/json")

	res, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

	defer res.Body.Close()
	body, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(res.Body)

	fmt.Println(res)
	fmt.Println(string(body))

}

HttpResponse<String> response = Unirest.post("https://metrics-api.nanostream.cloud/authenticate")
  .header("content-type", "application/json")
  .body("{\"email\":\"foo@bar.foo\",\"password\":\"secretFooBar\"}")
  .asString();

<?php

$client = new http\Client;
$request = new http\Client\Request;

$body = new http\Message\Body;
$body->append('{"email":"foo@bar.foo","password":"secretFooBar"}');

$request->setRequestUrl('https://metrics-api.nanostream.cloud/authenticate');
$request->setRequestMethod('POST');
$request->setBody($body);

$request->setHeaders([
  'content-type' => 'application/json'
]);

$client->enqueue($request)->send();
$response = $client->getResponse();

echo $response->getBody();

import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("metrics-api.nanostream.cloud")

payload = "{\"email\":\"foo@bar.foo\",\"password\":\"secretFooBar\"}"

headers = { 'content-type': "application/json" }

conn.request("POST", "/authenticate", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

require 'uri'
require 'net/http'
require 'openssl'

url = URI("https://metrics-api.nanostream.cloud/authenticate")

http = Net::HTTP.new(url.host, url.port)
http.use_ssl = true
http.verify_mode = OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_NONE

request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(url)
request["content-type"] = 'application/json'
request.body = "{\"email\":\"foo@bar.foo\",\"password\":\"secretFooBar\"}"

response = http.request(request)
puts response.read_body

```

Get a time series of byte usage for playout and ingest traffic with a maximum temporal resolution of an hour. If the asked hour is not yet completed, because the user given end date is in the future, you will receive the usage until the current elapsed time.

Constraint:
- start and end date have to point to a full hour e.g. 2026-01-14T15:00

Since this API route accesses low resolution data it offers some benefits compared to the high resolution usage API route:
- historical data (> last 3 months)
- longer time ranges are requestable
- response time is low

```

  Get statistics about conspicuous IPs (based on playback duration) ordered descending by the highest total playback duration. Includes detailed metrics for streams, sessions, and network information.
  Supported filters: Stream, IP, JTI, Referrer, Country, Provider, User, Tag

parameters.name: concurrency
parameters.description: Set true to enable concurrency metrics calculation (may takes a few more time)

streams.description: Filter by stream names (include only these streams)

ips.description: Filter by IP addresses (include only these IPs)

jtis.description: Filter by JWT token IDs (jti claim)

providers.description: Filter by internet service provider names

users.description: Filter by user IDs (user claim from JWT)

tags.description: Filter by tag values (include only sessions/streams with these tags)

orgaHash.description: Organization hash related to the IP

durationSum.description: Total playback duration in seconds related to the IP

durationAvg.description: Average playback duration in seconds related to the IP

sessionCount.description: Total session count related to the IP

streamCount.description: Total unique stream count related to the IP

tokenCount.description: Total unique playback token count related to the IP

topProviders.description: Top internet service providers associated with the IP

topCountries.description: Top countries where the IP is used from

topReferrers.description: Top referrers associated with the IP

topAgents.description: Top user agents associated with the IP

topTokens.description: Top playback token IDs (jti) used from this IP

streamStart.description: Start of the first stream related to the IP (ISO 8601 format)

streamEnd.description: End of the last stream related to the IP (ISO 8601 format)

concurrency.description:
Metric to measure the concurrency of playback
(Calculation: sum of total playback duration / (end of
the last playback - start of the first playback))

topStreams.description: Top streams (ordered by sum of playback duration)

durationSum.description:
Total playback duration in seconds related to the
stream

durationAvg.description:
Average playback duration in seconds related to the
stream

sessionCount.description: Total session count related to the stream

tokenCount.description: Total unique token count related to the stream

streamStart.description: Start of the first stream (ISO 8601 format)

streamEnd.description: End of the last stream (ISO 8601 format)

topAgents: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/91.0.4472.124 Safari/537.36

``` https://metrics-api.nanostream.cloud/v2/playback/start/success/ratio/timeseries ``` Get a time series of the playback start success ratio for all playbacks. Please note that this data is delayed by 4-5 minutes, so data for the current minute is not yet available. **How is the playback start success ratio defined:** During the start of a playback, it can happen that, for example, due to a poor connection of the viewer, not enough data can be loaded. After a short time, the player detects the insufficient data throughput and terminates the playback with an error. Other causes can also include: - wrong configuration of the player - stream to be connected is no longer being ingested - with active ABR: configured initial ABR profile demands a higher data throughput than what the viewer has available - further reasons for errors ... The playback start success ratio is determined from two values: Value 1: All playbacks that terminate with an error within the first 10 seconds after the initialization of playback. This does not include terminations after pausing and subsequent restart a playback. Value 2: All playbacks, regardless of whether they terminate with an error or not. The successful playback starts (Value 2 -Value 1) is compared to all playback starts, and the ratio is expressed as a percentage,
so the **playback start success ratio** is calculated as `100 * (Value2 - Value1) / Value2` **Note**: - **Important:** Due to the delay of data collection, do not expect to receive data for the last 4-5 minutes of the current minute. - to obtain data on this route the H5Live player must be configured to send metrics - the returned start errors cannot be compared with errors that can be queried, for example, via `/v2/monitoring/playout/errorcodes`, since just errors on the playback start are considered which means several filters are applied

count.description: The number of playbacks that terminate with an error within the first 10 seconds after the initialization of playback
The number of all playbacks, regardless of whether they terminate with an error or not

percent.description: The proportion of the number of playback starts from this bucket in relation to the sum of playback starts from all buckets in the array, expressed as a percentage.
The ratio in percent of playback start success -> ((playback start count - error count) * 100) / playback start count
